title: In five CMIP6 large ensembles, outcrop lightening lowers sigma0 26.5 oxygen in the western North Pacific but not off California, and no ensemble forces the 2006-2017 outcrop freshening
abstract: Question: is the 2006-2017 freshening that lightened the western North Pacific sigma0 26.5 winter outcrop box (OB, 38-48 N, 150-170 E) a forced change, and does outcrop lightening explain the size of the downstream oxygen loss on 26.5? Approach: CMIP6 initial-condition large ensembles read through ESGF (surface: 111 members of ACCESS-ESM1-5, CanESM5, MPI-ESM1-2-LR, IPSL-CM6A-LR, UKESM1-0-LL; 3-D O2: 44 members of four models), compared with a published WOD/Argo OB series. Member-minus-ensemble-mean anomalies give a natural experiment with the forcing held fixed. Tests were hashed before model data were read. Results: the forced 2006-2017 OB salinity change is -0.026 to +0.110 (observed -0.131). The raw member spread contains the observation in the three large ensembles (p 0.13-0.30), but model OB variability is 2-3.5 times the observed (Argo-era SD ratio 0.29-0.51); with the spread scaled to the observations the freshening is outside all five ensembles (p <= 0.011, exploratory). The models lighten OB by warming (forced 0.58-1.50 deg C by 2006-2017, observed 0.02-0.12). In all four O2 ensembles, internal OB lightening raises AOU on 26.5 at 160 E-180 within 0-2 yr (r -0.67 to -0.84; -50 to -96 umol/kg per kg/m3), less and later in the central and eastern gyre (lag 2-15 yr), and not significantly off California in 3 of 4 models. Model sensitivity times the observed lightening gives 0.33-0.58 of the observed western AOU gain, 0.03-0.10 in the transition zone and 0.01-0.03 off California (1 of 12 cases passes). Under SSP2-4.5 the OB does not return to its 1985-2005 density by 2045 in four models (MPI-ESM1-2-LR: chance 0.27-0.33). Limitations: small 3-D ensembles (9-14 members), one month per year, coarse grids with 26.5 too deep in three models, an exploratory variance correction, and model-dependent forced paths.
